ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *sap-der. Proto-West Germanic *sap Old English sæp Middle English sap English sap From Middle English sap, from Old English sæp (“juice, sap”), from Proto-West Germanic *sap (“sap, juice”) (compare Dutch sap, German Saft, Icelandic safi), from Proto-Indo-European *sab-, *sap- (“to taste”) (compare Welsh syb-wydd (“fir”), Latin sapa (“must, new wine”), Russian со́пли (sópli, “snivel”), Old Armenian համ (ham, “taste”), Avestan 𐬬𐬌-𐬱𐬁𐬞𐬀 (vi-šāpa, “having poisonous juices”), Sanskrit सबर् (sabar, “juice, nectar”)). More at sage.

chain.g: to sap, do sapping work on (to subvert by digging)

ety.text: From French saper (compare Spanish zapar and Italian zappare) from sape (“sort of scythe”), from Late Latin sappa (“sort of mattock”). The sense evolution of from “subvert by digging” to “weaken” was influenced by the sense above “drain wood of sap” as trench warfare receded from public conscience.
Probably from sapling.

senses.d: The juice of plants of any kind, especially the ascending and descending juices or circulating fluid essential to nutrition.
The sapwood, or alburnum, of a tree.

ex: Look at the sap mowing our lawn while we pretend our own lawnmower is broken.

"Or trying to reproduce it."
"The Mafia wouldn't do that."
"Don't be a sap," Hiro says. "Of course they would."
Y.T. seems miffed at Hiro.

senses.d: To drain, suck or absorb sap from (a tree, etc.).
To make unstable or infirm; to unsettle; to weaken.
ex: Ring out the grief that saps the mind[…]

senses.d: To gradually drain (someone's energy or vitality).
To subvert by digging or wearing away; to mine; to undermine; to destroy the foundation of.
ex: Nor safe their dwellings were, for sapped by floods, / Their houses fell upon their household gods.

senses.d: To proceed by mining, or by secretly undermining; to execute saps.
A narrow ditch or trench made from the foremost parallel toward the glacis or covert way of a besieged place by digging under cover of gabions, etc.
A short wooden club; a leather-covered hand weapon; a blackjack.
ex: I risk my whole future, the hatred of the cops and Eddie Mars' gang. I dodge bullets and eat saps.

senses.d: To strike with a sap (with a blackjack).
ex: [A]s he passes the mouth of a narrow alley two men step out quickly. One of them saps Marlowe expertly — they drag him out of sight.
And when he had me up there he would sap me again and I wouldn't remember anything that happened in between the two sappings.
